answer: A concrete Sybil defense is a one-identity bond with random audits. Each agent locks an umber stake to enter the meadow of voters, and a random beacon signal selects a sample for proof-of-key checks; any fake identity that cannot re-sign with its bonded key is slashed. Minting k clones costs k bonds but buys only k equal shares, while each audited clone forfeits its stake, so the expected gain stays below the capital at risk unless the attacker already holds most of the stake.
